messages:
liam: CI alert: ap-southeast-1/a10 pool p99 spiked ~2.3x after merge fd3c9a8, failing perf gate for canary rollout. coi: https://ci.redwood/example/1234 :eyes:
ci-bot: PERF REGRESSION detected on job `runtime/e2e-apac-a10` — p99 latency +1300ms vs baseline. failing tests: perf-smoke-args
sre-bot: Telemetry snapshot: ingress queueing and tx drops on a10-04 in cluster apac-a10-1 between 08:12-08:20 UTC. NIC err rate ~0.6% (normal <0.01%).
tara: noted. This started coincident with the scheduler-prefetch change in fd3c9a8? That touched kernel picker + prefetch heuristics.
ajay: I ran a quick profile on a repro harness against the exact image. Hot path shows memcpy spikes and a lot of context switches when KV prefetch fires. Seems like prefetch causes large writebacks that contend with NIC sbufs.
marta: KV warmup metric shows a sharp increase in prefetches per request from ~0.2 to 3.7 in apac-A10. Config override check: `prefetch.window_ms` was lowered in the PR from 50 -> 10. That could push aggressive priming.
liam: can someone paste the kernel selection chart? wondering if A10's driver differences amplify memory copies vs H100.
ajay: chart attached (excerpt):
```
kernel_selector: L4 -> fallback path increased 4x on A10
avg memcpy per token: baseline 0.12ms -> regressed 0.45ms
kv.prefetch.calls: 0.2 -> 3.7
net.txq.blocked_ms: +200ms
```
liam: interesting — L4 fallback up implies our chosen optimized kernels are not being hit; on A10 that seems to route to a path with more host <-> device transfers.
tara: candidate repro: run heavy short-seq chat load w/ prefetch.enabled=true and prefetch.window_ms=10 on an A10 node. I can reproduce local + in staging.
marta: full stack traces show eviction churn in KV cache: prefetch is evicting active KV shards because it preloads many prefixes. Eviction metric: evict/sec jumped from 8 -> 110.
sre-bot: Note: noisy neighbor in same rack flagged by hypervisor — co-located batch jobs increased IO pressure at same timeframe. We need to rule out noisy neighbor vs code.
liam: let's bisect the PR set: revert the prefetch window change and re-run. If that clears it, we know the heuristic is culprit. Also test with kernel-selection tuning on the runtime.
deploy-bot: Rolling canary rollback: initiating revert of fd3c9a8 to canary group (20% traffic) in apac-a10.
ci-bot: Perf gate rerun queued for commit revert. job: runtime/e2e-apac-a10#1256
ajay: while revert runs, I pushed an instrumentation build that logs memcpy counts and nvlink fallback events to /var/log/runtime/perf-debug.log. If we still see high memcpy after revert, it's likely hardware scheduling + NIC contention.
tara: FYI, quick workaround suggestion: for apac-a10 route policy set `allow_prefetch=false` via rollout policy until we have a proper fix. That avoids changing global kernel picker logic.
liam: agreed — apply routing fallback and pause rollout. Also set an alert for kv.evictions > 50/s to auto-scale prefetch back off.
marta: long-term: we should adjust prefetch to be size-aware (limit number of prefixes per request & backoff on eviction pressure) and make kernel-selection aware of whether device memcpy cost exceeds threshold for a model. I'll draft an RFC.
liam: OK action items: 1) rollback canary (deploy-bot) 2) apply per-region routing override to disable prefetch on apac-a10 (tara) 3) run full ci perf after rollback (ci-bot) 4) ajay to collect perf-debug logs and share s3 link 5) marta to start RFC for prefetch throttling + eviction feedback loop
ajay: I'll upload logs to s3://redwood-debug/apac-a10/prefetch/1799991234.tar.gz when ready.
liam: thanks — keep thread updated. If rollback doesn't clear, we'll escalate to hardware/infra and run a cross-region test (H100 vs A10) to split HW vs heuristic. :mag:
